Question B-008-005-001.

Why the correct answer is right: An ideal notch filter removes one narrow frequency while allowing other frequencies to pass. Think of cutting one small notch out of a smooth response curve.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Attenuate a range of frequencies and pass all others": Attenuating a range while passing others describes a band-reject or band-stop filter, not the ideal single-frequency notch.
- sourceIndex 2: "Attenuate all frequencies except one single frequency": Passing only one frequency while rejecting the rest is the opposite idea, closer to an ideal very narrow band-pass response.
- sourceIndex 3: "Attenuate all frequencies except a range of frequencies": Passing a range while rejecting frequencies outside it describes a band-pass filter, not a notch.
